Inventory is the asset that disappears when you sell it. Everything else on a balance sheet — machines, buildings, receivables — tends to persist. Inventory moves. And the moment it moves, it stops being an asset and becomes an expense: cost of goods sold. IAS 2 governs how that transition is measured, and the choices it demands have real consequences for reported profit. Get the cost wrong, miss an NRV write-down, or pick the wrong valuation method, and both sides of the financial statements are off.


## What Counts as Inventory?

IAS 2.6 defines inventories as assets held for sale in the ordinary course of business, in the process of production for such sale, or in the form of materials or supplies to be consumed in the production process or in rendering services. That threefold definition maps cleanly onto the types that appear on most manufacturing or retail balance sheets.

| Type | Examples |
|---|---|
| Raw materials | Steel, fabric, chemicals |
| Work in progress (WIP) | Half-finished components, partially assembled goods |
| Finished goods | Packaged product ready for delivery |
| Merchandise | Retail stock purchased for resale, unmodified |

The scope of IAS 2 has deliberate limits. Construction contracts fall under IFRS 15. Financial instruments are governed by IFRS 9. Biological assets — growing crops, livestock — belong to IAS 41. Commodity broker-traders may measure at fair value through profit or loss rather than cost. Everything else — the ordinary stock of a manufacturer, retailer, or service company — is squarely within IAS 2.

::: {.flip-card}
#### Inventory (IAS 2.6)
Assets held for sale in the ordinary course of business, in the process of production for such sale, or in the form of materials or supplies to be consumed in the production process or in rendering services.
:::

::: {.quick-check}
Which of the following falls **outside** the scope of IAS 2?

- Raw materials purchased for a production run
- Finished goods ready for delivery to customers
- **Growing timber on a forestry company's land**
- Merchandise held by a retail chain for resale
:::
